bihar_raw_news.title: Supreme Court to Hear Plea on Airfare and Airline Charges Today | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 07, 2026 SC to hear on September 7 plea seeking guidelines to control unpredictable fluctuations in airfare Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear on Monday a plea seeking regulatory guidelines to control the “unpredictable fluctuations” in airfare and ancillary charges imposed by private airlines in India. As per the apex court’s cause list of September 7, the matter would be heard by a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta. On August 17, the Centre had told the top court that it has fast-tracked the framing of rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, which is aimed at modernising India’s aviation sector, and the same would be finalised within three weeks. The government had placed the draft rules before the bench in a sealed cover and said some final discussions were going on. The apex court had noted that Additional Solicitor General Anil Kaushik, appearing for the Centre, sought three-week time to get the draft rules finalised and place it before the court. The top court is hearing a plea filed by social activist S Laxminarayanan, who has sought a robust and independent regulator that ensures transparency and passenger protection across the civil aviation sector and regulatory guidelines to control the “unpredictable fluctuations” in airfare and ancillary charges imposed by private airlines in India. Senior advocate Ravindra Srivastava, appearing for the petitioner, had argued before the bench that till the time the new rules come into force, the old rules are operating. Questioning the “lack of willingness” on the part of authorities and the effectiveness of the existing mechanism, he had argued that airlines were charging exorbitant fares. On July 13, the top court had asked the Centre to place the rules framed under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, before it. It had said the rules be placed before it in a sealed cover, irrespective of whether those have been placed before Parliament. While hearing the plea on May 15, the apex court said there should be some rationalisation of airfares and asked the Centre to provide relief to flyers. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who was then appearing in the matter for the Centre, had told the bench that the new enactment of 2024 had come into effect in January 2025 and the corresponding rules were in the process of being prepared. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

P. Radhakrishnan, launched the India Valve Registry on 5 September 2026 at the India Valves 2026 conference in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. The registry is a multicentre national database for secure and de-identified collection of real-world data on patient outcomes in heart valve interventions. India Valve Registry The India Valve Registry is designed to record clinical data from hospitals across India that perform valve interventions. It collects de-identified patient information, which is a standard method used in medical databases to protect personal identity while retaining clinical utility. Advanced heart valve interventions have been performed in India since 2011, but no continuous national database existed before this launch. The registry is intended to document regional clinical variation, patient age groups, and long-term treatment outcomes. India Valves 2026 Conference India Valves 2026 began on 4 September 2026 and was the 9th edition of India’s national forum on structural heart disease and transcatheter heart valve therapies. The complainant, Ashish Kumar of Bihar’s Jehanabad district, alleged that the accused projected himself as someone with access to senior politicians and government officials and used those claimed connections to gain his confidence. Police have booked the accused under Section 316(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with criminal breach of trust. No arrest has been publicly reported so far. He was later allegedly handed an appointment letter for the post of trainee district development officer. But the promised employment never materialised. This alleged appointment letter could become an important piece of evidence in the investigation. That payment trail will be central to the police investigation. Online transactions can establish dates, recipient accounts and amounts. Cash payments, however, are harder to prove and may depend on witnesses, messages, receipts or other supporting evidence. bihar_raw_news.title: India's TB Fight: How Indigenous Innovation Can Drive Tuberculosis Elimination
bihar_raw_news.content: September 07, 2026 Gearing up to eliminate tuberculosis Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Gobardhan Das | Simarjot Kaur For much of the developed world, Tuberculosis (TB) is a disease of the past. For India, it remains one of the country’s biggest public health and economic challenges. Nearly one in every four TB patients worldwide are from India, making the disease not just a healthcare concern, but a test of the nation’s scientific capability, policy execution and innovation ecosystem. As India is marching towards becoming a developed nation by 2047, eliminating TB is no longer simply about saving lives, it is about reducing healthcare costs and demonstrating India’s ability to solve a global problem through indigenous innovation. Over the past decade, India has significantly strengthened its fight against Tuberculosis (TB) through the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP). Although the ambitious 2025 elimination target remains a work in progress, it has accelerated investments in diagnostics, treatment and patient support. The results are encouraging. According to the WHO Global TB Report 2025, India’s TB incidence has declined by 21%, from 237 to 187 cases per lakh population between 2015 and 2024, almost twice the global rate of decline. During the same period, TB mortality fell by 25%, while treatment coverage improved dramatically from 53% to 92%, reflecting stronger case detection and better access to care. Digital platforms such as Ni-kshay, nutritional support through the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana, expanded molecular diagnostics and nationwide community campaigns under TB Mukt Bharat have together transformed India’s TB response, laying a strong foundation for eventual elimination. Despite this progress, the battle is far from over. Drug-resistant TB remains a serious threat, requiring longer treatment, higher costs and more complex clinical management. Delayed diagnosis, undernutrition, diabetes, overcrowded living conditions and social stigma continue to fuel transmission. Addressing these issues will require stronger public health systems alongside continued scientific innovation. Scientific innovation is changing the landscape of TB treatment. New medicines such as Bedaquiline, Delamanid and Pretomanid have significantly improved outcomes for patients with drug-resistant TB by enabling shorter and more effective treatment regimens. Researchers are also working on improved vaccines, rapid diagnostics and host-directed therapies that strengthen the body’s immune response against infection. India is not merely adopting these innovations; it is actively developing them. The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and its National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (NIRT) are leading research on new diagnostics, treatment strategies and disease surveillance. The Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) are supporting startups and research institutions working on vaccines, diagnostics and novel therapeutics, helping build a stronger indigenous innovation ecosystem. Indian industry is also playing a crucial role. Companies such as Macleods Pharmaceuticals, Lupin, Cipla and Cadila Pharmaceuticals manufacture affordable anti-TB medicines that are used across India and also exported to many low and middle-income countries. Meanwhile, Molbio Diagnostics has developed the portable Truenat platform, enabling rapid molecular diagnosis even in remote healthcare settings. bihar_raw_news.title: CM Shivakumar calls for deeper Indo-US ties in tech, innovation - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 07, 2026 CM Shivakumar calls for deeper Indo-US ties in tech, innovation Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Sunday called for deeper India-US cooperation in technology, education, innovation, research, investment and culture, pitching Bengaluru as a key technology and innovation hub in the strategic partnership between the two countries. Addressing an event marking the 250th anniversary of American independence, in the presence of US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, Shivakumar said the India-US relationship was moving beyond traditional government-to-government engagement, with universities, scientists, entrepreneurs, startups and businesses playing an increasingly important role. “Washington and New Delhi may guide the strategic partnership between our countries. But Bengaluru and Silicon Valley give it a powerful technological dimension,” he said. Shivakumar said Karnataka was keen to expand cooperation with the US in artificial intelligence, semiconductors, aerospace, advanced manufacturing, digital technologies and scientific research. “Karnataka’s ambition is to be among those who shape, build and lead the technologies of tomorrow,” he said. Highlighting economic ties, the chief minister said more than 1,000 American companies operated in Karnataka, accounting for nearly half of the total American corporate presence in India, while more than 80,000 American citizens lived in Bengaluru. “The strongest connection between our two countries will be built not only through commerce, but through knowledge, ideas and innovation,” Shivakumar said. The CM said Karnataka was building an ecosystem for next-generation technologies and investments, including KWIN City and a semiconductor park, besides plans for an AI tech park with an AI hub and India’s first public sector AI university. Shivakumar also highlighted the state’s growing presence in advanced manufacturing, aerospace and defence, saying Foxconn, which manufactures Apple iPhones, had its largest presence in India in Bengaluru. He said the state’s Aerospace Park was also expanding. Referring to Bengaluru’s emergence as a global technology and education hub, Shivakumar said the city had strengthened its role in India’s international engagement. “(Infosys founder) Narayana Murthy played an important role in shaping Bengaluru’s global journey, including his association with BIAL,” he said. Recalling former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s observation that while people once travelled to Delhi and Mumbai, “today, the world comes to Bengaluru”, Shivakumar said the city had become a major global gateway to India. “The world looks at India through Bengaluru,” he said. Shivakumar said Bengaluru has also emerged as a global education hub, with one of the highest concentrations of international schools in the country, and called for stronger educational and cultural exchanges between universities, institutions and young people in India and the US. Inviting American companies and institutions to explore investment opportunities under the state’s Beyond Bengaluru programme, Shivakumar said Karnataka offered access to talent, research capabilities, industrial infrastructure and a government willing to partner with investors. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that over the past several years, the relationship between India and France has reached new heights. He said, together with President Macron, both countries are building a Special Global Strategic Partnership. Speaking during inauguration of Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Paris through video conferencing, Mr Modi said, From technology, AI and defence to space and climate action, both nations are moving forward together with new momentum and renewed energy. He said, both sides also celebrating this year as the India-France Year of Innovation. The Prime Minister said, the India-France Strategic Partnership is special because it rests upon the strong foundation of the longstanding cultural and political connections. He said, history bears witness to the sacrifices of Indian soldiers in France, a history that continues to live in the collective memory and hearts. Mr Modi said, those interested in languages also know the important role French scholars have played in promoting and popularising Sanskrit. He said, the writings of Romain Rolland on Ramakrishna Paramahansa and Swami Vivekananda brought both societies even closer together. The Prime Minister said, from Paris to the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in Puducherry, The Mother’s spiritual journey inspired countless Indian and French seekers. He said, decades ago, Srila Prabhupada Swami also came to France and through ISKCON, he opened a new chapter in the spiritual relationship between India and France. Mr Modi said, today, yoga has also become an important medium of people-to-people connection between India and France. He said, the images from International Yoga Day in front of the Eiffel Tower are a wonderful example of the popularity of yoga in France. He added that now, through the magnificent BAPS Swaminarayan temple, a new chapter is being added to the India-France deep cultural relationship. The Prime Minister said, these days, there is much discussion about the possibilities of India-France joint ventures. He said, the Swaminarayan Temple has added a new dimension to this possibility as well. He added that this temple is Made in India and Built in France. Mr Modi said, a significant portion of the stone used in the temple was carved in India. He said, India’s ancient craftsmanship and talent have now come together with modern engineering in France. The Prime Minister hoped that this temple will stand for centuries as a symbol of cooperation and the immense possibilities that exist between India and France. He said, Swaminarayan temples have always been centres not only of devotion but also of service. Mr Modi expressed confidence that the cultural and spiritual messages that emanate from the temple will benefit people across Europe. He said, the temple will not only enrich the diversity of France, but will also bring renewed energy to the cultural relationship between India and France.

national_raw_news.title: 48 mins ago | Regional News 27 Delhi CM orders magisterial inquiry into Satya Niketan building collapse
national_raw_news.content: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the building collapse incident in Satya Niketan area of New Delhi, and directed registration of an FIR against the building owner. The Chief Minister’s Office said the decision was taken following an on-site review and a preliminary assessment of the incident. The CMO said those found responsible for the grave incident will be held fully accountable and dealt with under the strictest provisions of law. Death toll in the incident has risen to six following the recovery of one more body late last night. Search and rescue operations continued at the site as teams work to clear the debris and look for any trapped person. Teams from the NDRF, Fire Service, Delhi Police, and other agencies are working at the site to clear the debris. Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to Delhi Chief Minister, Delhi Police Commissioner and Director General of NDRF and assessed the situation on the ground. Mr Shah said, the injured are being provided with all necessary medical assistance. The building was being used as a paying guest accommodation. A senior police officer said repair work was underway in the basement when the structure collapsed at around 1.30 pm yesterday. Delhi Mayor Pravesh Wahi has said that all illegal constructions having more than four floors will be sealed with immediate effect. He said strict action will also be taken against officials found responsible, including their immediate dismissal. Sri Venkateswara College of the University of Delhi will remain closed today in the wake of the tragic building collapse. The college has said that, as a temporary measure, it is accommodating students in its classrooms following the closure of several paying guest accommodations and the sense of insecurity among students residing in the Satyaniketan area. Aryabhatta College has also suspended teaching today, in view of the building collapse. The college has been converted to a temporary shelter for students affected by the incident. However, teaching and non-teaching staff will remain available at the college to extend necessary assistance, cooperation and support to students during this difficult time.

national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 35 ISRO says space sector reforms focus on ecosystem expansion, not privatisation
national_raw_news.content: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has issued a clarification on reports circulating in the media regarding speculations and misinformation that there is an attempt to privatise ISRO or reduce its role. In a social media post, ISRO said that it will neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished. It added that participation of the private sector in space is aimed at enabling ISRO to focus even more strongly on the next generation of India’s space programme, while industry scales up mature technologies and capabilities. ISRO said the space-sector reforms aim to create a larger, stronger and globally competitive Indian space ecosystem. It said the reforms should therefore be seen as ecosystem expansion and capability multiplication, rather than privatisation. Noting the growth in India’s industrial and technological capabilities, ISRO said that mature and scalable activities can increasingly be undertaken by Indian industry. This would enable large-scale production, commercialisation, innovation and access to global markets, while allowing ISRO’s scientific and technical manpower to concentrate on advanced research, next-generation technologies and complex national missions. ISRO said this approach will allow it to devote more resources and scientific manpower to the next generation of technologies and missions, while the wider ecosystem provides the investment, manufacturing capacity and scale required by an expanding national space programme.

national_raw_news.title: J&K Folk Festival concludes in Ramban, showcasing Pahari cultural heritage 17 mins ago 5
national_raw_news.content: In Jammu and Kashmir, the two-day grand Folk Festival culminated last evening at the picturesque meadow of Sunaseri (Guglidhar) in Ramban district, showcasing the rich folk traditions, cultural heritage and ethnic identity of the Pahari community. The festival was organised by the locals, in collaboration with the District Administration Ramban, Directorate of Tourism Jammu and Jammu & Kashmir Academy of Art, Culture & Languages, with the objective of promoting indigenous culture and strengthening the potential of Sunsari as an emerging rural and eco-tourism destination. The festival witnessed enthusiastic participation from thousands of locals and visitors, who enjoyed traditional folk music, cultural performances and local ethnic cuisine, creating a vibrant atmosphere at the scenic destination. One the occasion MLA Ramban Arjun Singh Raju inaugurated newly developed tourism infrastructure and amenities, executed by the Public Works (R&B) Department at an estimated cost of 2.17 crore. The facilities include eco log huts, viewpoints, benches, improved drainage and connected pathways aimed at enhancing visitor amenities while maintaining the area’s natural ecology. He appreciated the District Administration and the local community for organising the festival and preserving the region’s rich cultural traditions. He described Sunaseri as one of the most picturesque yet unexplored destinations of Ramban and expressed his commitment to making the festival an annual feature after the monsoon season to attract more visitors. The two day festival featured colourful Pahari folk and cultural programmes, showcasing traditional music, dance and local art forms; rural sports competitions promoting the region’s indigenous sporting traditions; and camping activities that offered visitors an opportunity to experience the natural beauty and rural charm of Sunaseri.
